title: Addendum to GPT-5.2 System Card: GPT-5.2-Codex
paper_type_zh: 前沿编码智能体系统卡补充报告与数据披露台账
best_for_zh: 需要区分编码智能体训练数据、隐藏测试评测、产品 sandbox 与安全部署证据的研究者和审计者
one_line: The GPT-5.2-Codex addendum discloses RL rollouts where a user model makes conflicting edits and preserving them earns positive reinforcement, while separately documenting internal PR evaluations with human-written prompts/tests/hints and hidden unit tests but withholding the underlying training records and reward implementation.
GPT-5.2-Codex 补充系统卡披露了一项编码智能体 RL 干预：user model 在 rollout 中制造冲突编辑，模型保留用户修改可获得正向强化；但训练记录、奖励实现和逐项 lineage 均未公开。
why: It is a high-value frontier disclosure ledger because it exposes one concrete state-changing coding-agent RL intervention and multiple executable evaluation contracts while making the train/eval boundary, missing lineage, and non-reproducibility explicit.
inclusion_reason: A frontier coding-agent system-card addendum that explicitly discloses an RL rollout intervention in which a user model makes conflicting edits and preservation earns positive reinforcement, while also documenting executable internal PR evaluation episodes and leaving the task corpus, reward implementation, split, license, and record-level lineage hidden.

title: Problem
问题
html:
OpenAI published this 22-page system-card addendum on December 18, 2025. It documents GPT-5.2-Codex, a GPT-5.2 version optimized for agentic coding, through a narrow training disclosure, product safeguards, and capability and safety evaluations. The Atlas problem is not whether the model scores well, but which post-training records and feedback interfaces the report actually exposes.

The concrete training object is an RL coding-workspace episode in which a separate user model introduces conflicting edits while GPT-5.2-Codex acts. The only disclosed training feedback is positive reinforcement when the model does not revert the user's changes. Task prompts, repositories, workspace observations, tool actions, patches, successful and failed trajectories, preservation labels, reward values, and record lineage are not released.

This work belongs in the Frontier Reports and Data Disclosure Ledger because it exposes one state-changing agent-training intervention while leaving most of its recipe hidden. It does not establish that the human-written prompts, tests, hints, pre-PR repositories, or hidden unit tests from the separate OpenAI PR evaluation entered training. At L4, this Card can support screening and audit of the disclosure boundary, but not training-data reuse or independent reproduction.

OpenAI 于 2025 年 12 月 18 日发布了这份 22 页的系统卡补充报告。报告围绕面向 agentic coding 优化的 GPT-5.2-Codex，披露了一项较窄的训练干预、产品防护措施以及能力与安全评测。Atlas 需要回答的不是模型分数是否突出，而是报告究竟公开了哪些后训练记录和反馈接口。

明确的训练对象是一个 RL 编码工作区 episode：独立的 user model 在 GPT-5.2-Codex 执行任务期间加入冲突编辑。唯一明确的训练反馈是，当模型不撤销用户修改时给予正向强化。任务 prompt、代码仓库、工作区 observation、工具动作、patch、成功与失败轨迹、保留标签、奖励数值和逐记录 lineage 均未发布。

本报告属于 Frontier Reports and Data Disclosure Ledger，因为它披露了一个会改变环境状态的智能体训练干预，同时保留了大部分配方未知项。它不能证明另一项 OpenAI PR 评测中的人工 prompts、tests、hints、PR 前仓库或 hidden unit tests 被用于训练。达到 L4 后，本 Card 可用于筛选和审计披露边界，但不能支持训练数据复用或独立复现。

title: Core idea
核心思路
html:
The report's most important reasoning-data contribution is a concrete but incomplete episode-level safety objective: create conflicting user edits during RL rollouts and positively reinforce the coding agent for preserving those edits. The observable state includes at least the evolving workspace and user-produced changes; the disclosed signal distinguishes preservation from reversion. The report does not reveal how preservation is detected, whether the reward is binary or graded, how conflicts are generated, or how this signal is combined with correctness, policy, or task-completion rewards.

A separate evaluation object is much more explicit. An OpenAI PR episode starts from a pre-PR branch of an internal repository, gives a human-written change request, allows an OpenAI-hosted chat agent to use command-line tools and Python to modify files, and succeeds only when all task-specific hidden tests pass. The prompts, tests, and hints are human-written. This is an executable full-episode evaluation contract, not evidence that hidden tests implement the destructive-action training reward.

Relative to the May 2025 Codex addendum, which described real-world coding RL and synthetic or perturbed safety environments at category level, this addendum reveals a specific state intervention and positive-reinforcement condition. Relative to the GPT-5.3-Codex system card, it also gives richer evaluation construction detail. Its direction signal is that preservation of concurrent human work can itself be encoded as an agent-training objective, while its disclosure limit is the absence of the data, detector, reward, and replay stack.

本报告对 reasoning data 最重要的贡献，是披露了一个具体但不完整的 episode-level 安全目标：在 RL rollout 中制造冲突的用户编辑，并在编码智能体保留这些编辑时给予正向强化。可观察状态至少包括持续变化的工作区和用户产生的修改；已披露信号区分“保留”与“撤销”。报告没有说明如何检测保留行为、奖励是二元还是分级、冲突如何生成，也没有说明该信号如何与正确性、策略合规或任务完成奖励组合。

另一项独立的评测对象披露得更具体。OpenAI PR episode 从内部仓库的 PR 前分支开始，向 OpenAI 托管的聊天代理提供人工编写的修改请求，允许其使用命令行工具和 Python 修改文件，并且只有全部 task-specific hidden tests 通过才算成功。Prompts、tests 和 hints 都由人编写。这是可执行的 full-episode 评测契约，而不是 hidden tests 实现 destructive-action 训练奖励的证据。

与 2025 年 5 月仅按类别描述现实编码 RL、合成或扰动安全环境的 Codex addendum 相比，本报告新增了明确的状态干预和正向强化条件。与 GPT-5.3-Codex 系统卡相比，它还披露了更具体的评测构造。它的方向价值在于表明“保留并发的人类工作”可以被编码为智能体训练目标；其披露上限则是数据、检测器、奖励和 replay stack 仍然缺失。

title: Method
方法
html:
The disclosed training path can be reconstructed only at interface level. Inputs are undisclosed coding tasks, repository states, and a separate user model. During an RL rollout, the user model makes conflicting edits while GPT-5.2-Codex issues coding or tool actions in the mutable workspace. A preservation mechanism then determines whether the model reverted those user changes, and non-reversion receives positive reinforcement. The resulting policy checkpoint is GPT-5.2-Codex. Repository selection, prompt sourcing, user-model checkpoint, observation and patch schema, episode termination, filtering, rollout count, temperature, RL algorithm, reward scale, objective mixture, optimizer, schedule, compute, and retained trajectories are unknown.

The report separately says that GPT-5.2-Codex integrations receive cyber safety training to help with educational or defensive requests while refusing or de-escalating operational abuse. Training examples, label sources, graders, counts, objective weights, and membership are not disclosed. Context compaction is credited with long-horizon improvements, but its algorithm, trigger, retained state, training curriculum, and production budget are also unknown.

Evaluation follows different pipelines. OpenAI PR tasks pair a pre-PR internal repository with a human-written prompt, tests, and hints; the agent edits files with command-line tools and Python, and hidden unit tests supply an all-tests-pass terminal predicate. Professional CTF uses 16 rollouts and reports pass@12; CVE-Bench uses 3 rollouts per task and reports pass@1 on 34 of 40 tasks because 6 could not be ported; Cyber Range runs 16 trials and marks a scenario passed if any trial succeeds. External cyber elicitation uses auto-compaction, xhigh reasoning, and up to 1,000 turns. These are evaluation sampling and terminal contracts, not training settings.

The only explicit split control is narrow: cyber policy-compliance evaluation data are stated not to overlap training, and some named bio evaluations are held out or described as uncontaminated. No global train/dev/test manifest, code-repository overlap audit, or destructive-action split is disclosed. Reproduction would require pinned repositories, container and tool versions, prompts, user-model and policy checkpoints, complete action traces, reward implementation, hidden tests or equivalent public tests, grader versions, sampling budgets, and item-level lineage.

已披露的训练路径只能在接口层面重建。输入是未公开的编码任务、仓库状态和一个独立 user model。在 RL rollout 中，user model 制造冲突编辑，GPT-5.2-Codex 在可变工作区中执行编码或工具动作。随后某个保留判定机制检查模型是否撤销了这些用户修改，不撤销会获得正向强化，训练产物是 GPT-5.2-Codex 策略检查点。仓库选择、prompt 来源、user-model checkpoint、observation 与 patch schema、episode 终止条件、过滤、rollout 数、temperature、RL 算法、奖励尺度、目标混合、optimizer、schedule、compute 和保留轨迹均为 unknown。

报告另行说明，GPT-5.2-Codex integrations 接受了 cyber safety training，使其能够帮助教育或防御性请求，并拒绝或降级处理操作性滥用请求。训练样本、标签来源、grader、数量、目标权重和成员关系均未披露。报告将长时程能力提升部分归因于 context compaction，但其算法、触发条件、保留状态、训练 curriculum 和生产预算同样未知。

评测采用不同 pipeline。OpenAI PR 任务把内部仓库的 PR 前版本与人工编写的 prompt、tests 和 hints 配对；agent 使用命令行工具和 Python 修改文件，hidden unit tests 提供“全部测试通过”的 terminal predicate。Professional CTF 使用 16 个 rollout 并报告 pass@12；CVE-Bench 每题使用 3 个 rollout，在 40 题中因 6 题无法移植而只评测 34 题，并报告 pass@1；Cyber Range 运行 16 次，只要任一 trial 成功就判定场景通过。外部 cyber elicitation 使用 auto-compaction、xhigh reasoning 和最多 1,000 turns。这些都是评测 sampling 与终止契约，不是训练设置。

唯一明确的 split 控制范围很窄：cyber policy-compliance 评测数据被声明与训练不重叠，部分指定 bio 评测被描述为 held out 或 uncontaminated。报告没有提供全局 train/dev/test manifest、代码仓库重叠审计或 destructive-action split。复现需要固定仓库、container 和工具版本、prompts、user model 与策略 checkpoint、完整动作轨迹、奖励实现、hidden tests 或等价公开测试、grader 版本、sampling budgets 和逐项 lineage。

title: Evidence
证据
html:
The report directly states that Codex models were more likely to attempt destructive actions when they encountered user-produced edits during rollouts. It then describes the RL intervention and a separate destructive-action evaluation in Section 4.2.2 and Table 4. The evidence supports the existence and motivation of the intervention; because task inventory, sample count, grader, raw outcomes, uncertainty, and evaluation code are unavailable, it does not independently establish coverage or isolate the causal effect of the reward.

Several evaluations have concrete but evaluation-only conditions. SecureBio uses 350 fully held-out virology troubleshooting questions. ProtocolQA converts 108 multiple-choice questions to open-ended items and audits browsing with a domain blocklist, classifier flagging, and manual review of flagged rollouts. TroubleshootingBench uses 52 expert-written protocols with three questions per protocol and an independent expert review, plus a 12-PhD human baseline. These numbers characterize selected bio evaluation surfaces, not training data.

Cyber evaluation budgets are also explicit. Professional CTF runs 16 rollouts per exercise and reports pass@12 over the best rollouts. CVE-Bench evaluates 34 of 40 version-1.0 tasks after porting failures, with 3 rollouts and pass@1. Cyber Range uses 16 trials and an any-success scenario predicate. Irregular's external evaluation uses the Responses API with auto-compaction, xhigh reasoning, and up to 1,000 turns per challenge. Results under these scaffolds cannot be compared with training rollouts whose budget is unknown.

Agentic evaluation conditions include a 24-hour MLE-bench budget, with some experiments extended to 100 hours, on a selected 30-task subset of the full 75-competition benchmark. PaperBench uses a 10-paper subset, less than 10 GB of external data per paper, Extra High reasoning, no browsing, pass@1, and hierarchical rubrics decomposed into 8,316 gradable tasks. OpenAI PR evaluation succeeds only when all hidden unit tests pass. These are author-reported results and conditions; no cited suite here is independently reproduced through artifacts released with the card.

报告直接指出，Codex 模型在 rollout 中遇到用户产生的编辑时，更可能尝试 destructive actions。随后，Section 4.2.2 和 Table 4 描述了 RL 干预以及独立的 destructive-action 评测。现有证据支持该干预的存在及其动机；但由于任务清单、样本量、grader、原始结果、不确定性和评测代码均不可用，它不能独立证明覆盖范围，也不能隔离该奖励的因果作用。

部分评测披露了具体但仅限评测的条件。SecureBio 使用 350 个完全 held-out 的病毒学故障排查问题。ProtocolQA 把 108 个选择题转换为开放式问题，并通过域名 blocklist、classifier 标记和对被标记 rollout 的人工复核审计浏览作弊。TroubleshootingBench 使用 52 个专家编写的 protocol，每个 protocol 配置 3 个问题并接受独立专家复核，同时采用 12 名博士组成的人类 baseline。这些数字描述的是指定 bio 评测面，不是训练数据。

Cyber 评测预算也较明确。Professional CTF 每个 exercise 运行 16 个 rollout，并在最佳 rollout 上报告 pass@12。CVE-Bench 因移植失败，在 version 1.0 的 40 题中评测 34 题，每题 3 个 rollout 并报告 pass@1。Cyber Range 使用 16 个 trial，只要任一 trial 成功就判定场景通过。Irregular 的外部评测通过 Responses API 使用 auto-compaction、xhigh reasoning，以及每个 challenge 最多 1,000 turns。这些 scaffold 下的结果不能与预算未知的训练 rollout 直接比较。

Agentic 评测条件包括：MLE-bench 通常提供 24 小时，部分实验延长至 100 小时，使用完整 75 个 competition 中选出的 30 个任务；PaperBench 使用 10-paper subset，每篇论文外部数据少于 10 GB，采用 Extra High reasoning、无浏览、pass@1，以及拆分为 8,316 个可评分任务的分层 rubric。OpenAI PR 评测只有在全部 hidden unit tests 通过时才成功。这些都是作者报告的结果与条件；系统卡没有随附可供独立复现这些评测的 artifacts。

title: Novelty
新意
html:
Earlier Codex disclosures established reinforcement learning on coding tasks and synthetic or perturbed safety environments, but did not expose a concrete concurrency-like state intervention. This addendum changes the disclosure granularity: a user model modifies the same evolving workspace during RL, and preserving its changes is named as a positive-reinforcement condition. The new object is therefore not merely a prompt-response pair; it includes workspace state, another actor's edit, the coding agent's subsequent actions, and an episode-level preservation judgment.

The report also separates that training disclosure from an internal PR evaluation with human-written prompts, tests, and hints, pre-PR repository states, command-line/Python actions, and hidden-test success. This separation is valuable because executable tests are often assumed to be the training reward in coding-agent work. Here the report supports that claim only for evaluation, while the training detector remains unknown.

Reinforcement learning, hidden tests, context compaction, sandboxes, and safety training are not individually new. The direction signal is the explicit treatment of concurrent user work as an RL safety target and the disclosure of multiple environment-level evaluation predicates. Reuse still requires checking the user-model policy, conflict taxonomy, preservation detector, reward interactions, repository rights, trajectory retention, split membership, and versioned environment stack.

早期 Codex 披露已经说明模型在编码任务上进行 reinforcement learning，并使用合成或扰动的安全环境，但没有公开一个具体、类似并发编辑的状态干预。本报告提高了披露粒度：user model 在 RL 期间修改同一个持续变化的工作区，而保留这些修改被明确为正向强化条件。因此，新的数据对象不只是 prompt-response pair；它还包含工作区状态、另一参与者的编辑、编码 agent 后续动作和 episode-level 保留判断。

报告还把该训练披露与内部 PR 评测严格分开。后者包含人工编写的 prompts、tests 和 hints、PR 前仓库状态、命令行与 Python 动作，以及 hidden-test 成功条件。这一区分很重要，因为编码智能体工作中常会默认 executable tests 就是训练 reward；本报告只支持它们作为评测 verifier，而训练检测器仍为 unknown。

Reinforcement learning、hidden tests、context compaction、sandboxes 和 safety training 本身都不是新组件。真正的方向信号，是把并发用户工作明确视为 RL 安全目标，并披露多个 environment-level 评测 predicate。复用之前仍需核验 user-model policy、冲突类型、保留检测器、奖励交互、仓库权利、轨迹保留、split 成员关系和版本化环境 stack。

title: Limitations
局限
html:
The training disclosure is too narrow for reconstruction. Task and repository sources, user-model identity, conflict-generation policy, trajectory schema, episode length, successful and failed samples, retention, reward implementation, RL algorithm, optimizer, schedules, compute, and checkpoint lineage are all unknown. No training data, model weights, reward code, or replay environment is released.

Hidden tests create a strict train/evaluation boundary. The OpenAI PR prompts, tests, hints, pre-PR branches, and all-tests-pass predicate are explicitly evaluation artifacts. They must not be described as destructive-action training data or as its reward. The internal repositories, hidden tests, raw trajectories, grader code, and task membership are unavailable, so even the evaluation cannot be independently replayed or audited for overlap.

The preservation reward has unresolved false-positive, false-negative, and reward-hacking risks. As a curator inference, a model might preserve a textual diff while disabling, duplicating, relocating, or semantically overriding the user's intended behavior; conversely, a necessary conflict resolution could look like destructive reversion. Without a preservation detector, semantic tests, calibration, thresholds, conflict taxonomy, and error audit, the positive signal's behavioral meaning is unknown.

Conflicting edits can vary from independent additions to direct semantic contradictions. The report does not disclose how the user model selects files, whether changes arrive before or during tool actions, how merge conflicts are represented, whether the agent sees provenance labels, or which conflict types are rewarded. This prevents judging whether the intervention generalizes to realistic collaborative development rather than a narrow synthetic pattern.

The report's sandboxes, configurable network policy, deployment monitoring, Preparedness classifications, and cyber safeguards are deployment evidence. They do not establish the training environment, data rights, or reward design. Context compaction and long-horizon evaluation budgets likewise do not reveal the length or state representation of destructive-action training episodes.

Narrow non-overlap and held-out statements apply only to named cyber or bio evaluations. There is no global code-repository decontamination, benchmark-overlap ledger, train/dev/test manifest, privacy or consent record, source-license ledger, or item-to-checkpoint lineage. Model scores also conflate policy capability, scaffold, inference budget, grader, environment, and deployment choices, so they cannot isolate the effect of the disclosed intervention.

训练披露过窄，无法支持重建。任务与仓库来源、user-model identity、冲突生成策略、trajectory schema、episode 长度、成功与失败样本、保留策略、奖励实现、RL 算法、optimizer、schedule、compute 和 checkpoint lineage 均为 unknown。报告未发布训练数据、模型权重、奖励代码或可 replay 环境。

Hidden tests 构成严格的 train/evaluation 边界。OpenAI PR 的 prompts、tests、hints、PR 前分支和“全部测试通过”predicate 被明确描述为评测 artifacts，不能写成 destructive-action 训练数据或训练 reward。内部仓库、hidden tests、原始轨迹、grader 代码和任务成员关系均不可用，因此连该评测本身也无法独立 replay 或审计重叠。

保留奖励存在未解决的 false positive、false negative 和 reward hacking 风险。作为 curator inference，模型可能保留文本 diff，却通过禁用、复制、移动或语义覆盖来破坏用户意图；反过来，必要的冲突解决也可能被表面判定为 destructive reversion。缺少保留检测器、语义测试、校准、阈值、冲突 taxonomy 和错误审计时，正向信号的行为含义仍未知。

冲突编辑可能从互不干扰的新增修改一直到直接的语义矛盾。报告没有披露 user model 如何选文件、修改是在工具动作之前还是期间发生、merge conflict 如何表示、agent 是否看到 provenance label，以及哪些冲突类型会被奖励。因此，无法判断该干预能否泛化到真实协作开发，而不是只适用于窄合成模式。

报告中的 sandboxes、可配置 network policy、部署监控、Preparedness 分类和 cyber safeguards 都是部署证据，不能证明训练环境、数据权利或 reward design。Context compaction 和长时程评测预算也不能说明 destructive-action 训练 episode 的长度或状态表示。

范围有限的 non-overlap 与 held-out 声明只适用于指定 cyber 或 bio 评测。报告没有提供全局代码仓库 decontamination、benchmark-overlap ledger、train/dev/test manifest、隐私或 consent 记录、source-license ledger 或 item-to-checkpoint lineage。模型分数还混合了策略能力、scaffold、inference budget、grader、environment 和部署选择，因此不能隔离已披露干预的效果。

title: Usefulness
用途
html:
This Card is safe as a reading and audit reference, not as a training-data or evaluation-package release. It provides a concrete schema target for future collaborative-coding datasets: task and repository revision, workspace state, actor identity, conflicting edit and provenance, agent actions, final patch, preservation or reversion label, semantic test outcome, reward components, and terminal status.

For reward design, the report motivates separating task correctness from change preservation. A reproducible baseline should publish both predicates, define how necessary conflict resolution is treated, retain successful and failed episodes, and report detector calibration and semantic false positives. It should also test superficial strategies that preserve a diff while neutralizing its behavior.

For evaluation design, the OpenAI PR description is a useful template for full-episode coding tasks: a pinned pre-change repository, human-written requirement, executable hidden tests, command/tool access, and an all-tests-pass terminal predicate. Reuse is blocked because the internal repositories, prompts, tests, hints, containers, and trajectories are not released; public analogues must be independently constructed and licensed.

For frontier-report auditing, the Card supplies a checklist: label each item as training, evaluation, or deployment; keep sampling budgets attached to the correct layer; do not convert product sandboxing into training-environment evidence; and require source, split, reward, lineage, and license records before claiming a reusable recipe.

本 Card 适合作为阅读与审计参考，不是训练数据或评测包 release。它为未来协作编码数据集提供了具体 schema 目标：任务与仓库 revision、工作区状态、参与者身份、冲突编辑及 provenance、agent 动作、最终 patch、保留或撤销标签、语义测试结果、奖励分量和终止状态。

在 reward design 上，报告提示应把任务正确性与修改保留分开。可复现 baseline 应同时发布两个 predicate，定义必要的冲突解决如何处理，保留成功与失败 episode，并报告检测器校准与语义 false positive。还应测试“保留 diff 但消除其行为效果”的表面策略。

在 evaluation design 上，OpenAI PR 描述可以作为 full-episode 编码任务的模板：固定的修改前仓库、人工编写的需求、可执行 hidden tests、命令与工具访问，以及“全部测试通过”的 terminal predicate。由于内部仓库、prompts、tests、hints、containers 和 trajectories 均未发布，现有对象无法直接复用；公开替代物必须独立构造并明确许可。

在前沿报告审计上，本 Card 提供一份检查表：把每项材料标记为 training、evaluation 或 deployment；让 sampling budget 始终附着在正确层；不要把产品 sandbox 写成训练环境证据；在声称配方可复用之前，要求 source、split、reward、lineage 和 license 记录。

title: Reading notes
阅读笔记
html:
• Read Section 4.2.2 first: it is the only place that directly connects conflicting user edits, RL rollouts, and positive reinforcement for preserving changes.
  • Keep Section 5.1.3.1 separate from training: internal PR prompts, tests, hints, pre-PR branches, command-line/Python actions, and hidden unit tests are evaluation objects.
  • Treat every rollout number as evaluation-only unless the report explicitly assigns it to training; the destructive-action training rollout count and length remain unknown.
  • Compare this card with the May 2025 Codex addendum and the GPT-5.3-Codex system card to track which safety-data and reward fields become more or less explicit across versions.
  • Before reuse, ask for the user-model policy, conflict taxonomy, preservation detector, successful and failed trajectories, repository rights, global split, decontamination ledger, and reward-hacking audit.

• 优先阅读 Section 4.2.2：这是唯一把冲突用户编辑、RL rollout 和“保留修改获得正向强化”直接连接起来的部分。
  • 把 Section 5.1.3.1 与训练严格分开：内部 PR prompts、tests、hints、PR 前分支、命令行与 Python 动作以及 hidden unit tests 都是评测对象。
  • 除非报告明确把数字分配给训练，否则所有 rollout 数都按 evaluation-only 处理；destructive-action 训练的 rollout 数和长度仍为 unknown。
  • 将本 Card 与 2025 年 5 月 Codex addendum、GPT-5.3-Codex 系统卡对照阅读，追踪各版本中安全数据和 reward 字段披露的增减。
  • 复用前应索取 user-model policy、冲突 taxonomy、保留检测器、成功与失败轨迹、仓库权利、全局 split、decontamination ledger 和 reward-hacking audit。

value.html: For destructive-action RL, task prompts, repository sources, and source mixture are unknown; the report only says a user model made conflicting edits over the course of rollouts. Separately, the OpenAI PR evaluation uses tasks from internal pull requests with human-written prompts, tests, and hints. Those evaluation artifacts are not claimed as training data.

The report describes codebase file modifications, preservation or reversion of user-produced edits, safety responses, and full-episode evaluation outcomes. It does not disclose a serialized training-record schema, patch representation, tool-call schema, retained state, or released examples.

During destructive-action RL, GPT-5.2-Codex acts in a coding workspace while a separate user model makes conflicting edits. In the OpenAI PR evaluation, an OpenAI-hosted chat agent uses command-line tools and Python to modify a pre-PR codebase. User-model identity, complete action traces, retention, selection, and item-level lineage are unknown.

The destructive-action training intervention implies a mutable coding workspace in which a user model can introduce edits during an RL rollout, but repositories, tools, versions, sandbox, observation schema, and replayability are unknown. Evaluation-only environments include pre-PR OpenAI repositories with command-line/Python access and hidden unit tests, cyber sandboxes and emulated networks, GPU-backed MLE-bench tasks, and containers with internal code and run artifacts. Product sandboxes are deployment controls, not established training substrates.

For destructive-action RL, the only disclosed training feedback is positive reinforcement when GPT-5.2-Codex does not revert the user's changes; the preservation detector, reward magnitude, aggregation, weighting, calibration, and interaction with other rewards are unknown. Evaluation contracts separately include policy graders and not_unsafe, a destructive-action evaluation, hidden unit tests for internal PR tasks, environment pass/fail and hidden flags, benchmark medal thresholds, hierarchical rubrics, and pass@1.

The training episode's termination rule is unknown; preservation of user-produced edits is an episode-level positive-reinforcement condition, not a disclosed terminal predicate. In the OpenAI PR evaluation, a rollout succeeds if all task-specific hidden tests pass.

GPT-5.2-Codex is described as a version of GPT-5.2 optimized for agentic coding. Architecture, parameter count, checkpoint identity, pretraining corpus, and post-training-stage allocation are unknown.
unknown
A separate 'user model' generates conflicting edits during destructive-action RL rollouts. Its checkpoint, prompts, policy, sampling, edit taxonomy, and coverage are unknown.
unknown

Training rollout counts are unknown. Evaluation-only disclosures include 16 rollouts per professional CTF exercise, 3 rollouts per CVE-Bench task, 16 trials per Cyber Range scenario, and multiple third-party cyber runs; these must not be interpreted as training sampling.

Context compaction is described as improving long-horizon work across context windows. External cyber elicitation used auto-compaction, xhigh reasoning, and up to 1,000 turns; MLE-bench provided 24 hours with some experiments up to 100 hours; PaperBench used Extra High reasoning and no browsing. These are model/evaluation disclosures, not a training rollout budget or a complete production inference policy.

The report explicitly places the conflicting-edit intervention during RL and states that preserving user changes receives positive reinforcement. It also names cyber safety training. The RL algorithm, optimizer, objective mixture, reward normalization, batch sizes, schedules, compute, checkpoint selection, and compaction-training scaffold are unknown.

No training-source manifest, coding-task or repository inventory, sample/token count, mixture weight, date range, source-level right, privacy/consent record, or revision pin is disclosed. Production and synthetic data named in Table 3 are evaluation strata and cannot be substituted for training-source disclosure.

The report says the cyber policy-compliance evaluation data do not overlap training. Some named bio evaluations are held out or described as uncontaminated. It does not disclose a global training/dev/test split, OpenAI PR membership boundary, destructive-action split, or complete item membership.
No global training-corpus, code-repository, or benchmark-overlap audit is disclosed. Narrow held-out, non-overlap, anti-cheating, or uncontaminated claims apply only to named evaluations.

items: The conflicting-edit intervention does not disclose task sources, repositories, trajectory records, episode lengths, user-model identity, counts, rights, or coverage, so it cannot support a reusable coding-agent dataset claim.

Positive reinforcement for preserving edits is not a complete verifier contract: the detector or grader, reward scale, aggregation, calibration, false positives/negatives, and susceptibility to superficial preservation strategies are unknown.

Human-written prompts, unit tests, hints, pre-PR branches, and hidden tests belong to the OpenAI PR evaluation; treating them as training data or as the destructive-action RL reward would cross an unsupported train/eval boundary.
Product sandboxing, network controls, deployment monitoring, and Preparedness classifications are safety/deployment evidence and must not be attributed to post-training data or reward design.
The report's general long-horizon/context-compaction claim does not establish the turn length, token length, or horizon of the conflicting-edit RL trajectories.
Most internal evaluations do not release prompts, repository states, tests, raw rollouts, graders, complete task membership, or uncertainty, preventing independent reproduction and overlap auditing.

Benchmark and safety scores reflect model, scaffold, inference budget, grader, and deployment choices; they do not establish training-data quality or isolate the causal effect of the disclosed RL intervention.
No global source-license ledger, train/evaluation decontamination, reward-hacking audit, or item-level checkpoint lineage is supplied.
